canonical_question: Are the SKP measurements taken after the molten salt exposure or on the pristine as-cast surfaces, and how does this affect the interpretation of micro-galvanic corrosion?

question_variants.question: Are the SKP measurements taken after the molten salt exposure or on the pristine as-cast surfaces, and how does this affect the interpretation of micro-galvanic corrosion?
question_variants.resolution_summary: SKP measurements were taken on the pristine as-cast surfaces to understand micro-galvanic corrosion before exposure, not after.

answers.answer: The Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) analysis was performed on the pristine as-cast surfaces to measure the relative electron work function and understand micro-galvanic corrosion mechanisms. The text states: 'Phase-specific work function for the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 and DS2205 was measured to understand the micro-galvanic corrosion'. This indicates the measurements reflect the initial state, not the state after molten salt exposure.
answers.material: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy and DS2205
answers.measurement_outcome: Relative electron work function measured via SKP on as-cast surfaces.
answers.mechanism: Work function differences in the pristine state are used to infer micro-galvanic corrosion tendencies.
answers.boundary_limitation: None specific to the timing question.
evidence_spans: Here, the corrosion behavior of AlCoCrFeNI 2.1 EHEA in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl 2 salt was investigated at 450 °C and 650 °C.
The performance of EHEA was compared with one of the benchmark dual-phase structural alloys, namely duplex steel 2205 (DS2205).
To explain the effect of eutectic microstructure on the local electrochemical activity, Scanning Kelvin Probe (SKP) analysis was utilized to measure the relative electron work function
